newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Monday on the heels of an uneventful performance in London overnight, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures were off highs in rangebound trade at midday, with September up three stg at 1,024 stg a tonne, traded 1,028 to 1,023 stg. December rose one stg to 1,052 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures ended higher in a technical correction to recent sharp losses. September settled up $21 at $1,481 per tonne after ranging between $1,484 and $1,462. Second-month December rose $17 to $1,521, while the back months ended up $13 to $14.
Technically, traders said September faces some resistance near $1,485, followed by $1,500. Support was seen at Thursday's close of $1,460.

On the fundamental side, Ivory Coast's 1996/97 (October-September) cocoa crop is set to reach 1.15 million tonnes, slightly below last year's record, the government daily newspaper Fraternite Matin said.
